transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Yeah… I’m here because lately I’ve been having these times where I eat way more than I meant to. Like after a long shift, or after studying, I’ll grab a full fast-food meal, then snacks, then whatever’s in the fridge, all in one sitting. It’s been bothering me.
Can you tell me if, during these eating episodes, you feel like you can’t stop eating or control what or how much you’re eating?

Yeah. Once I start on those nights, it really feels like I can’t stop. Like I’ll be telling myself, “Okay, that’s enough,” and my hands just keep grabbing more food anyway, even when I’m already feeling sick.
Do these eating episodes make you feel very upset, guilty, or ashamed afterward?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I know I don’t feel good about it after, but I haven’t really stopped to sort out if it’s guilt or shame exactly. It just feels… bad, and I’d rather not think about it too much.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate for what you’ve eaten?

Yeah… sometimes I do. After I eat too much, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. Other times I’ve taken laxatives. It’s mostly because I get scared about what all that food is going to do to me.
